//: Release automation, driven by the Conventional Commits already in use.
Commits are routed to a package by the FILES they touch, not by the commit
scope — so the existing mix of component scopes (web/api/android) and issue
scopes (#214) all land in the right changelog with no change to how commits
The four deployables deliberately do NOT share a version. api/web are
continuously deployed services where exactly one version exists at a time and
semver communicates nothing to anyone; their releases exist for traceability
(a tag + changelog answering 'what shipped when'). android/ios are INSTALLED
artifacts: old versions live on user devices for months, so their semver is
real and their release notes are user-facing.
Build NUMBERS are not managed here — versionCode / CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION
come from the git commit count at build time (monotonic by construction, see
mobile.yml). This file owns only the human-facing marketing version.
